subject: Alligator snapping turtle
hook: ALLIGATOR SNAPPING TURTLE IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Despite their reputation as fearsome predators that decimate fish populations, alligator snapping turtles are actually significant seed dispersers that consume large volumes of acorns.
angle_support: Between March and October, stomach samples of 65 turtles showed that 56% of their diet by volume was composed of acorns of water, overcup, and willow oaks.
As ingested willow oak acorns were found to germinate faster after defecation, it is suggested that alligator snapping turtles may be important seed dispersers of oak trees.
title: The Surprising Diet of the Alligator Snapping Turtle
description: Contrary to popular belief, alligator snapping turtles are not just fish-eating monsters. They play a critical ecological role by dispersing oak tree seeds throughout their habitats.
narration: ALLIGATOR SNAPPING TURTLE IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture a terrifying, armored predator that exists solely to wipe out local fish populations with its legendary, bone-crushing bite. It is a common reputation for this prehistoric-looking giant, but the reality of their diet is far less focused on hunting than you might assume. While they are capable of snapping through solid objects, fish actually make up a surprisingly small portion of their intake. Data shows that fish account for only seven percent of their diet by volume. Instead, these turtles are major plant eaters. Remarkably, over half of their stomach content consists of acorns. Because they consume these seeds and travel, they actively help oak trees spread their range upstream and laterally, acting as vital forest gardeners rather than just aquatic hunters. The feared ambush predator is actually a crucial, wandering farmer of the southeastern American river systems.
